correctness.rationale: For every orthonormal tangent pair, the cubic restriction has only first and third Fourier modes, with third coefficient exactly one-eighth of the product of three complex coordinate projections per block. The curvature-radius form is therefore radius minus twice the real block-amplitude sum. The AM--GM and disjoint orthogonal-energy inequalities give the sharp bound \(\rho-(4\sqrt6/9)B\); a balanced single-block tangent pair attains equality, proving necessity as well as sufficiency. Equality enforces one balanced block, yielding exactly 12 curvature-singular normals per maximum-amplitude block, each with one null tangent direction. The Fourier planar-area identity gives the exact shadow law, and the same strict equality allocation gives the complete 4-per-block minimum-plane classification. The proof is analytic and covers all real coefficients, dimensions, and planes; 29,819 finite checks passed as supplementary evidence. Boundary cases \(B=0\) and endpoint convexity are separately specified.
